target_customer: Engineering teams building iOS, Android and web apps, especially teams using coding agents
problem: End-to-end testing is brittle and slow to maintain, and coding agents ship features faster than teams can verify them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for agent-run end-to-end tests
product_category: AI end-to-end testing for mobile and web apps

founders.name: Yuvan Sundrani
education: University of Maryland (per the university article, as a computer science alumnus)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and University of Maryland CS article seen in search results.

founders.name: Jason Steinberg
prior_employers: Founding teams of several mobile-first startups (not named)
education: University of Maryland (per the university article, as a computer science alumnus)

competitors.name: Maestro
competitors.what: Open source mobile UI automation framework

competitors.name: Appium
competitors.what: Widely used open source mobile end-to-end testing framework

technical_complexity.rationale: Vision-based agents driving real devices and adapting to UI changes, with CLI, MCP and PR integrations; standard engineering with hard reliability problems.

defensibility.rationale: Many AI testing entrants; test suites and CI integration give some lock-in, SOC 2 helps enterprise sales.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy found in sources; Autosana itself acquired Meadow, a customer profile testing platform, on 23 June 2026 per its blog.

market_need_then: Coding agents sped up feature output in 2025, making testing the bottleneck; roundups in 2025 describe agentic mobile test tools as a fast-growing category.

branding.name_origin: Press says the name is Latin for self-healing, tied to tests that adapt as the product changes (company-sourced claim)

identity.logo: Wordmark Autosana beside a small app icon
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct action headlines such as Catch bugs before your users do.

branding.community_and_virality: Maintains a blog with SEO roundups ranking itself first; named customer logos shown on site.

brand_strength.rationale: Name has a self-healing story that matches the product, but no evidence of brand-driven growth beyond product marketing.

outcome_analysis: Autosana raised a 3.2M USD seed in February 2026 led by YC after the Summer 2025 batch, shows named customers like Life360, Kalshi and Partiful, and acquired Meadow in June 2026. Timing with coding agents helps. Competition from many AI testing tools is the main risk, and company growth claims are unverified.
notes: Round confirmed by two outlets (SiliconANGLE and Pulse 2), both seen via search snippets and not opened. NeuronFeed lists 3.7M across two rounds and StartupHub lists 3M; a tracker shows a Jan 2025 seed of 500K tied to YC, unverified. The Meadow acquisition is by Autosana, not of Autosana, so exit is none. Founder education for both comes from a University of Maryland article seen in search results; the YC page itself lists none. Competitor entries come from 2025 roundups, not launch-date comparisons. Customer metrics are self-reported.
